name: Chart Loader
description: Beatmaps as data: parsing, validating, and serving chart files with their difficulty tiers. Charts are read-only content — they are loaded, never written — which is why this sits in persistence next to the save system rather than in world or ui: the boundary it guards is 'bytes on disk become trustworthy structs', the same boundary as every other loader in the category. It owns the registry, difficulty selection, and validation, because a malformed note time discovered mid-song is a crash with an audience; failing at load with a named reason is this component's whole job. It deliberately does not own runtime note flow — ui.note_highway turns the loaded chart into motion — and it does not own the tempo map's meaning, which utility.beat_clock interprets against the audio clock. Storage mechanics defer to persistence.datastore_safe; charts are content, but the read path should be the safe one everywhere.

inputs.name: chartRegistry
inputs.description: Available charts: id, title, audio reference, and per-difficulty chart data. The registry is content inventory — what the song select screen lists.

inputs.name: defaultDifficulty
inputs.description: Tier used when a chart is requested without one. The tier names are chart metadata, not code — a pack can ship easy/normal/hard/expert or its own ladder.

inputs.name: validateOnLoad
inputs.description: Whether note times, lanes, and the bpm map are checked before the chart is served. Disabling it ships broken charts to the highway; there is no good reason outside a content-debug build.

inputs.name: maxNotesPerChart
inputs.description: Validation ceiling that catches truncated or runaway files. A three-minute chart at expert density is a few thousand notes; ten times that is a corrupt file, not a hard song.

outputs.name: loadedChart
outputs.description: The validated chart struct: notes with beat times and lanes, bpm map, metadata. This is the only shape the highway accepts.
